mil3.1.11:1.1: “How, venerable sir, does faith have the characteristic of leaping in?”
mil3.1.11:1.2: “Just as, Great King, a meditator, seeing the minds of others liberated, leaps forward toward the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-return, or the fruit of non-return, or arahantship, and applies himself to attain what has not been attained, to reach what has not been reached, to realize what has not been realized.
mil3.1.11:1.3: That, Great King, is how faith has the characteristic of leaping in.”
mil3.1.11:2.2: “Just as, Great King, a great cloud might pour down rain on a mountain top, and that water, flowing along the slope, would fill the mountain clefts, gullies, and branches and fill the river; the river would flow along, overflowing both banks. Then a great crowd of people would come and, not knowing whether the river is shallow or deep, frightened and rooted to the spot, would stand on the bank. Then some man would come and, seeing his own strength and power, would tightly gird up his loins, leap in, and cross over; and seeing that he had crossed over, the great crowd would cross over too;
mil3.1.11:2.3: so too, Great King, a meditator, seeing the minds of others liberated, leaps forward toward the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-return, or the fruit of non-return, or arahantship, and applies himself to attain what has not been attained, to reach what has not been reached, to realize what has not been realized.
mil3.1.11:2.4: That, Great King, is how faith has the characteristic of leaping in.
mil3.1.11:2.5: This too, Great King, was said by the Blessed One in the excellent Saṁyutta Nikāya—
mil3.1.11:5.1: The Question on Faith with the Characteristic of Leaping In: Eleventh.
